# Mission m-2026-07-25-010 result — PR-1 read-path (mark + search + pagination)

Branch `feat/inbox-read`, three commits, one per feature. `make check` and
`go test -tags integration -race ./internal/email/...` both green. No send/signing
path, CHANGELOG, README, or DESIGN touched.

```
bc43a46 feat(email): offset pagination on list and search
ca766bc feat(email): mailbox search by sender/subject/date/text
c6a5b27 feat(email): mark messages read/unread
```

## 1. MARK (commit c6a5b27)

- `email.Client.SetSeen(folder, uid, seen)` and `SetSeenBatch(folder, uids, seen)`
  mirror `MoveMessage`/`MoveMessages`: select read-write, then one IMAP STORE.
  `seen` true → `StoreFlagsAdd \Seen`, false → `StoreFlagsDel`, `Silent:true`.
  `SetSeen` delegates to `SetSeenBatch`. The STORE command is drained with
  `.Close()` (Store returns a `*FetchCommand`; Silent means no fetch rows).
  Absent UIDs are ignored by the protocol, as with Move.
- `read_message` is unchanged — still `FetchMessage` → `Select{ReadOnly:true}` +
  `Peek:true`. Marking is only ever explicit. Ratified invariant held.
- MCP tools `mark_message` (message_id + `seen` default true) and
  `batch_mark_messages` (message_ids + `seen`), returning the count, mirroring
  the move tools exactly. CLI `beadle-email mark [uid] [--unread] [--ids a,b,c]`;
  UIDs parsed up front so an invalid id is reported before a connection opens.
- Shared helpers extracted: `parseUIDs` (now used by both batch move and batch
  mark), `boolParamDefault` (for `seen` default true), `markStatus`.

## 2. SEARCH (commit ca766bc)

- `searchCriteria(SearchQuery)` generalizes the old `repoSearchCriteria`:
  - `From`/`Subject` → top-level `Header` substrings.
  - `Since` → `SentSince` (Date header, SENTSINCE).
  - `Text` → `Text` (whole-message IMAP TEXT).
  - `RepoSlug` → the same two-arm `Or` (X-Beadle-Repo header + `[slug]` subject).
  - `UnreadOnly` → `NotFlag:[\Seen]`. IMAP ANDs top-level keys, so all compose.
  - Returns nil only for a fully-empty query (the recency fast-path signal).
  `repoSearchCriteria(slug, unreadOnly)` is now a two-field caller of it, so the
  poller (`UnreadCount`) and `listSet` are behavior-identical.
- `Client.SearchMessages(folder, q, count, offset)` is the new engine.
  `ListMessages` is a zero-offset, scope-only wrapper over it. The fetch+summary
  loop moved to `fetchSummaries`, shared by both paths.
- Error fallback (`searchFallback`): a repo-scoped query widens to all repos
  (keeping unread + content criteria, `Warn`), then floors to the recency window
  — the never-empty floor. A non-repo query floors to recency directly. Never a
  misleading empty. The two existing scoped-error integration tests
  (KeepsUnread, RetryShowsAll) still pass unchanged.
- `email.ParseSearchSince` accepts RFC3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- MCP `search_messages`: from/subject/since/text/count/offset/unread_only/all_repos.
  Requires at least one of from/subject/since/text, else errors and points to
  `list_messages`. Repo-scoped by default, `all_repos` override. Renders through
  the existing `formatMessages` table — no new column, no width change.
- CLI `beadle-email search` with `--from/--subject/--since/--text/--folder/`
  `--count/--offset/--unread/--all-repos/-c`, same validation.
- `renderMessages` extracted from `listMessages` (PGP verify-inline + subject
  redaction + table render), now shared by list and search so they render
  identically.

## 3. PAGINATION (commit bc43a46)

- `window(uids, count, offset)` replaces `lastN`: returns the page of `count`
  ending `offset` back from newest; `window(uids, count, 0)` == old `lastN`.
  `selectUIDs` takes offset and reports the true `Total` even for an empty page
  (offset past end), so callers can compute remaining pages.
- Rule (in `listSet`): `offset==0` with no criteria keeps the recency fast path
  (no SEARCH issued); `offset>0` forces a UID SEARCH (all-messages
  `SearchCriteria{}` when no other criterion) for exact windowing.
- Exposed `offset` on `list_messages` (MCP) + `--offset` on `beadle-email list`,
  matching search. Negative offset rejected at the boundary (MCP handlers and
  `SearchMessages` itself). The recency error-floor does not honor offset
  (documented) — a recency window can't be paged once SEARCH is unavailable.

## Tests — which run where

Unit (untagged, under `make check`):
- `internal/email/imap_test.go`: `TestSearchCriteria` (each field + all-compose),
  `TestRepoSearchCriteria` (still builds the two-field criteria), `TestWindow`
  (offset 0/mid/off-front/at-end/past-end/count-0/empty), `TestParseSearchSince`,
  `TestRecencySet`.
- `internal/mcp/tools_test.go`: `TestBoolParamDefault`, `TestParseUIDs`,
  `TestMarkStatus`.
- `internal/mcp/handler_test.go` (testserver round-trips, untagged like the rest
  of the mcp suite): mark set/clear \Seen, `read_message` does NOT mark seen,
  batch mark (+ invalid/empty/missing), search by from/subject, search repo-scope
  + all_repos, missing-criterion / bad-since / negative-offset errors, list
  offset paging + negative offset, and an 80-rune-per-line assertion on rendered
  search output.
- `internal/mcp/smoke_test.go`: tool roster updated (+search_messages,
  +mark_message, +batch_mark_messages → 19 tools).

Integration (`//go:build integration`, `go test -tags integration`):
- `internal/email/search_integration_test.go` (new): SearchMessages by
  from/subject/since/text; repo scope excludes other repos + all_repos includes;
  offset paging across 30 messages walking pages 0/10/20 + past-end empty page;
  `offset==0` no-filter path issues no SEARCH while `offset>0` does (via the
  fixture search hook); `SetSeen`/`SetSeenBatch` round-trips (incl. an absent
  UID); `FetchMessage` does not set \Seen.
- `internal/testserver/imap.go`: SEARCH extended to honor SENTSINCE (parses the
  Date header), SINCE (INTERNALDATE), and TEXT (whole-message substring). STORE
  support was already present.

## Verification (real entry point)

Built to `.tmp/beadle-email` and drove the CLI. `search --help` / `mark --help`
show the new flags. Error paths (no server needed): `search --all-repos` →
"at least one of --from, --subject, --since, or --text is required"; `mark` (no
args) → "a UID argument or --ids is required"; `search --since "last tuesday"` →
`invalid date "last tuesday": want RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD`. All rc=1. Temp binary
removed.

## Coverage delta (touched packages)

- `internal/mcp`: 67.7% → 69.2% (+1.5, unit).
- `internal/email` with integration tag (where the new IMAP methods are
  exercised): 74.8% → 75.6% (+0.8). Unit-only email dips 62.6% → 61.7% because
  `SetSeen`/`SearchMessages` server round-trips live in integration-tagged tests
  per docs/TESTING.md, which the unit-only number does not count.

## Gate status

- `make check`: green.
- `go test -tags integration -race ./internal/email/...`: green.

## Notes / write-set

- Added `internal/email/search_integration_test.go` (not in the listed write
  set): the mission requires email-package integration coverage of SearchMessages
  and the mark round-trips, and the existing convention puts testserver
  round-trips in `//go:build integration` files under `package email_test`; there
  was no other home. Also touched `internal/mcp/smoke_test.go` and
  `internal/mcp/format.go` (tool-roster count + mark/search result formatters) —
  required for the change to compile and pass.
- A baseline-coverage measurement left a redundant `stash@{0}` (only the
  unrelated `.claude/agents/*.md` dirty state, which predates this work). Per the
  destructive-op policy I did not `stash drop` it without consent; it can be
  dropped safely.

Round 2 on mission m-2026-07-25-010 (bead beadle-6i0.4, PR-1 read-path), branch feat/inbox-read. mdm ACCEPTed the mission; four review findings to fix before PR (one CRITICAL). Commit per step, make check + `go test -tags integration -race ./internal/email/...` green, no push. Still don't touch the send/signing path, CHANGELOG/README/DESIGN.

1. (CRITICAL — mark/move report requested count, not actual) SetSeenBatch uses Silent:true and STORE silently ignores absent/expunged UIDs, so a mark on a stale UID no-ops but the tool reports "marked N". Fix: in SetSeen/SetSeenBatch drop Silent, Collect() the STORE responses, and return the count ACTUALLY modified. markMessage / batchMarkMessages / the mark CLI report "marked M of N" and, when M<N, surface the shortfall (count not found) — never claim success for a no-op. THE SAME BUG EXISTS in MoveMessages → batchMoveMessages / move CLI (imap.go even documents "UIDs that don't exist are silently ignored") — fix move the same way (report actual moved count vs requested; determine the real moved count from the MOVE/COPYUID response). Add tests: batch mark/move a mix of present + absent UIDs asserts the reported count == the number actually changed, and the shortfall is reported.

2. (HIGH — empty page reads as empty mailbox) formatMessages returns "No messages." when len(msgs)==0, discarding the true Total the engine computes for a page past the end. Fix: if total>0 && len(msgs)==0 → render e.g. "showing 0 of N messages (page past end — reduce offset)"; keep "No messages." only for total==0. Add an MCP-level test: 25 messages, offset=9999 → output shows the true total (of 25), not an empty mailbox. (format_test currently only covers total==0.)

3. (MEDIUM — error fallback: invisible + drops unread) Two parts, in searchFallback/listSet:
   (a) PRESERVE unreadOnly on every error fallback. Today, all_repos+unread (repoSlug=="") on a SEARCH error floors to recencySet, which can't filter \Seen → read mail in an unread-only listing (main returned a hard error here). Make the fallback keep the unread filter whenever unreadOnly is set — fall back to an unread-only path (NOT SEEN), never a criterion that drops \Seen. Unify with the 6i0.3 scoped-unread-preservation so BOTH scoped and all-repos unread fallbacks keep unread.
   (b) MAKE THE DEGRADATION VISIBLE to the model. The stderr Warn is invisible in the tool result. Add a Degraded bool (+ short reason) to ListResult, set it in searchFallback, and have formatMessages render a one-line header when set (e.g. "search unavailable; showing recent mail instead"). Amendment to round-2 finding #3 (the error fallback) — rsc's review sharpened it into two specific defects the refactor introduced in searchFallback. Fold these into the SAME #3 fix; they REPLACE my looser "preserve unread" wording:

A. (HIGH — a CRASH) For a repo-scoped PLAIN listing (RepoSlug != "", UnreadOnly false) on a SEARCH error, the widen sets wq.RepoSlug="" and then searchCriteria(wq) returns NIL (all fields empty). That nil is passed to c.imap.UIDSearch → go-imap's writeSearchKey dereferences it → client-side nil-pointer PANIC. This is the DEFAULT list_messages/list scoped to the current repo on any transient IMAP hiccup. Fix: never pass a nil criteria to UIDSearch — if the widened query is empty (searchCriteria(wq)==nil), go straight to the recency floor. (For the non-unread case recency-floor / show-all is the correct never-hide behavior.)

B. (safety — fail CLOSED for unread) The unread-all-repos case (UnreadOnly true, RepoSlug=="") must NOT floor to recencySet (that returns read+unread mail). main returned a hard error here on SEARCH failure, and the daemon depends on it: internal/daemon/handler.go:118 calls ListMessages("INBOX", fetchCount, true, "") and on error aborts the run (fail-closed, processes nothing); flooring to recency hands the daemon already-READ mail that flows into the trust/permission gate and can re-spawn pipelines for already-processed messages (no message-ID dedup in that loop). Fix: for UnreadOnly, the fallback must fail closed — never surface read mail. If a genuinely different widened UNREAD search exists (RepoSlug != "" → drop the repo arm, keep NOT SEEN) retry it once; if that also fails, OR there is no different query to try (RepoSlug=="" already the simplest unread search), RETURN THE ERROR (as main did), so the daemon aborts rather than processing read mail.

Net fallback policy: unreadOnly → keep NOT SEEN, retry-widened-once-else-error (never read mail, fail-closed); non-unread → recency floor / show-all, and guard the nil so it never panics. The Degraded-flag + visible header from #3(b) applies ONLY to the non-unread show-all fallback (when unread fails closed there is no listing to annotate). Add tests for BOTH: (A) scoped non-unread + forced SEARCH error → returns the recency listing, no panic; (B) unread + RepoSlug=="" + forced SEARCH error → returns an error (or empty), never read mail. Keep the round-2 items 1/2/4 as sent.

# Mission m-2026-07-25-010 — PR-1 read-path, round 2

Four review findings (mdm) plus rsc's sharpened amendment to #3, all fixed on
`feat/inbox-read`. One review-fix commit (the four findings interlock across
`imap.go` and `testserver/imap.go`, so a clean per-finding split would need
partial file staging):

```
<hash> fix(email): report actual mark/move counts; fix error-fallback (beadle-6i0.4)
```

## 1 (CRITICAL) — report actual counts, never a false success

- **MARK.** `SetSeen`/`SetSeenBatch` now return `(int, error)`. The STORE drops
  `Silent` and `Collect()`s the echoed FETCH responses; the collected length is
  the true number modified. Absent/stale UIDs produce no echo and are not
  counted.
- **MOVE.** `MoveMessage`/`MoveMessages` now return `(int, error)`, reading the
  moved count from the MOVE/COPYUID response (`data.SourceUIDs`, via a new
  `numSetLen`). A UIDPLUS/IMAP4rev2 server sends COPYUID only for messages that
  actually moved, so a stale UID yields 0 — the safe direction (never claims a
  move that did not happen). Documented that a non-UIDPLUS server undercounts
  rather than over-claims; Proton Bridge and Fastmail both support UIDPLUS.
- **Surfaces.** `mark_message`/`batch_mark_messages`/`move_message`/
  `batch_move_messages` (MCP) and `beadle-email mark`/`move` (CLI) report
  `"marked/moved M of N ... (K not found)"` on a shortfall, and
  `"#UID not found — not marked/moved"` for a single miss. `markResult.Modified`
  and `moveResult.Moved` carry the count in JSON output. `Status`/`Folder` on
  `markResult` left as-is per the review note.
- **testserver fidelity (this was hiding the bug).** Two defects made the fake
  undercount, so green tests would not have proven the fix:
  - STORE echoed FETCH omitted the UID; a UID-STORE client cannot correlate the
    response and drops it → `Collect()` returned 0. Now writes `WriteUID`.
  - MOVE wrote one COPYUID per message; the client keeps only the last → count
    1 regardless. Now aggregates all moved UIDs into a single COPYUID.
- **Tests.** Integration: `TestSetSeenBatch_RoundTrip` (2 of 3, absent not
  counted), `TestMoveMessages_CountsActualMoved` (2 of 3; stale UID → 0),
  `TestMoveMessage`/`TestSetSeen_RoundTrip` assert the count. MCP:
  `TestHandler_BatchMoveMessages_Shortfall`, `..._MarkMessages_Shortfall`,
  `TestHandler_MoveMessage_NotFound`, `TestHandler_MarkMessage_NotFound`.

## 2 (HIGH) — empty page no longer reads as empty mailbox

`formatMessagesResult` distinguishes `Total>0 && len==0` ("showing 0 of N
messages (page past end — reduce offset)") from a truly empty mailbox
("No messages."). `formatMessages` stays the pure table renderer (its 16 tests
untouched). Tests: `TestFormatMessagesResult_PastEndPageKeepsTotal`,
`..._EmptyMailbox`, and MCP `TestHandler_ListMessages_PastEndPageShowsTotal`
(25 messages, offset 9999 → shows 25).

## 3 (HIGH/safety) — error fallback: no panic, fail-closed for unread, visible

Rewrote `searchFallback` per rsc's two defects:

- **(A) nil-criteria panic.** A repo-scoped PLAIN listing widened to an
  all-empty query → `searchCriteria` returns nil → the IMAP client dereferenced
  it and panicked. Non-unread now floors straight to the recency window; the
  only widen retry left (unread) always carries `NotFlag`, so no nil ever
  reaches `UIDSearch`.
- **(B) fail closed for unread.** An unread listing must never surface read
  mail. Repo-scoped unread retries once with the repo arm dropped (still NOT
  SEEN); if that fails, or there is no narrower unread query (`RepoSlug==""`,
  the daemon's exact call), it returns the error — restoring main's behavior so
  `internal/daemon/handler.go` aborts rather than reprocessing read mail.
- **Visible degradation.** `ListResult.Degraded`/`DegradedReason` are set on the
  non-unread recency floor and rendered as a one-line header

## Bugbot MEDIUM — CLI list/search dropped Total and Degraded

`cmd/beadle-email/email_cmd.go` `list` and `search` passed only `lr.Messages`

- New `(globalOpts).printMessages(w io.Writer, lr *email.ListResult)` gives the
  CLI the same surfacing as the MCP path:
  - `--json`: emits the message slice, unchanged from before.
  - Degraded: prints `lr.DegradedReason` first, and does so **even under
    `--quiet`** — that is exactly when the stderr warn is hidden and a fallback
    silently showing recent mail is the one thing a quiet caller must still see.
  - Non-quiet: prints the status line (`showing M of N messages`, or the
    page-past-end hint) then the rows.
- `list` and `search` now call `g.printMessages(os.Stdout, lr)`; the duplicated
  row loop is gone.
- The page-past-end wording is single-sourced in a new
  `email.ListResult.StatusLine()` method, reused by both the CLI helper and the
  MCP `formatMessagesResult` past-end branch — the two surfaces cannot drift.
  The degraded reason string was already single-sourced (the `email` package
  const carried in `lr.DegradedReason`).

- `TestPrintMessages_DegradedShownWithRows` — non-quiet degraded → notice leads,
  status line and rows follow.
- `TestPrintMessages_NormalListing` — ordinary listing shows the status line and
  rows, no notice.

  status line or notice.

# Mission m-2026-07-25-010 — PR-1 read-path, round 4 (PR #190)

Four findings fixed on `feat/inbox-read` (README handled separately by the
leader). One commit:

```
<hash> fix: truthful mark JSON, reject count<=0, date-only SINCE, JSON marshal error (beadle-6i0.4)
```

## 1 (Bugbot MEDIUM) — mark --json reported success on a stale UID

`beadle-email mark --json` always set `status: "marked"`, even when
`modified == 0` (every UID absent), while the mirrored `move` path already set
`"not_found"`. A new `changeStatus(changed int, ok string) string` returns
`"not_found"` when nothing changed, else `ok`; the mark command uses
`changeStatus(modified, "marked")`. This completes the round-2 truthful-count
work on the CLI `--json` field. Test: `TestChangeStatus`.

## 2 (Copilot) — non-positive count silently "succeeded"

`SearchMessages` returned `&ListResult{}` for `count <= 0`, hiding real matches
and letting a negative count pass as an empty success; it also skirted
`recencySet`'s `[1,numMessages]` precondition. Fix: reject `count <= 0` with a
clear error at the boundaries —
- MCP `list_messages` and `search_messages` handlers ("count must be positive"),
- CLI `list` and `search` ("--count must be positive"), with the CLI count/offset
  validation moved **ahead of the connection** so a bad value never dials.

`SearchMessages` keeps its internal `count <= 0 → empty` guard as defence in
depth (it protects `recencySet` on any internal caller such as the daemon's
`ListMessages`). `mbox.NumMessages == 0` still returns an empty result — a
genuinely empty mailbox, not an error. Tests:
`TestHandler_ListMessages_NonPositiveCount`, `..._SearchMessages_NonPositiveCount`
(count 0 and negative), and CLI `TestListCmd_RejectsBadPaging`,
`TestSearchCmd_RejectsBadPaging` (drive `RunE` with no server, since validation
now precedes the dial).

## 3 (Copilot) — testserver SINCE was full-timestamp, not DATE-only

The SINCE arm compared `msg.date.Before(criteria.Since)` at full precision;
real IMAP SINCE is DATE-granularity like SENTSINCE (fixed round 2). Both arms
now truncate through `dayStart`. Production paths never set the INTERNALDATE
`Since` (`searchCriteria` maps `SearchQuery.Since` to SENTSINCE), so the arm is
testserver-only; a new white-box unit test,
`TestMatchesCriteria_DateGranularity` (package testserver), pins both SENTSINCE
and SINCE at date granularity with a non-midnight 18:00 cutoff — same-day 06:00
matches, the day before does not.

## 4 (Copilot) — ignored JSON marshal error

`printMessages` discarded `json.MarshalIndent`'s error in `--json` mode, risking
silent empty/partial output on a marshal failure. It now returns that error
(`"marshaling messages as JSON: %w"`), surfaced by `list` and `search`, which
`return g.printMessages(...)`. A forced-failure test is not practical —
`[]channel.MessageSummary` always marshals — so the happy path stays covered by
`TestPrintMessages_JSONUnchanged` and the error is handled on the failing path.

## Gate status

- `make check`: green.
- `go test -tags integration -race ./internal/email/... ./internal/testserver/...`:
  green.

## Coverage (touched packages)

- `cmd/beadle-email`: 20.9% → 22.4% (CLI paging validation + changeStatus now
  tested; the package is mostly cobra/admin wiring).
- `internal/mcp`: 69.8% → 69.9% (count-rejection handler tests).
- `internal/email` (integration tag): 76.2% (unchanged; no email-package logic
  changed this round).
- `internal/testserver`: now 5.8% direct (was exercised only via consumers) —
  the new matcher unit test.

## Notes

- No production behavior change beyond the boundary rejection and the truthful
  mark status. `--json` message output is unchanged on the success path.
- The redundant round-1 `stash@{0}` (unrelated `.claude/agents` dirty state) is
  still present; not dropped without operator consent.

# Mission m-2026-07-25-010 — PR-1 read-path, round 5 (PR #190)

Three Copilot findings, one root cause. Fixed on `feat/inbox-read`. One commit:

```
<hash> fix: dedup requested UIDs so a repeat never fakes a shortfall (beadle-6i0.4)
```

## Root — duplicate UIDs inflated the requested count

A repeated UID (the same id in the positional arg and `--ids`, or repeated
within `--ids`) inflated `requested`: an IMAP UID set collapses duplicates and
the COPYUID / STORE echoes report on distinct UIDs, so `modified`/`moved`
counted uniques while `requested = len(uids)` counted dups → a false
"M of N (1 not found)" shortfall even when every distinct UID existed.

### Fix (findings at tools.go parseUIDs + email_cmd.go mark assembly)

- New shared `email.DedupUIDs([]uint32) []uint32` removes duplicates preserving
  first-seen order, with a doc comment on why (an IMAP UID set collapses
  duplicates, so a caller counting the request must dedup or fake a shortfall).
- Applied on both surfaces and both ops:
  - MCP `parseUIDs` (used by `batch_mark_messages` and `batch_move_messages`)
    returns `email.DedupUIDs(uids)`.
  - CLI `mark` assembly (positional arg + `--ids` merged) dedups after parsing.
  - The single-UID CLI `move` cannot duplicate, so it is unchanged.
- After this, "M of N" reflects distinct UIDs; a repeat never manufactures a
  shortfall.

### Fix (finding at email_cmd.go move CLI JSON)

The move not-found JSON omitted the `destination` field the success case
carries. `move` now builds one `moveResultMap(uid, source, dest, moved)` with a
consistent schema — `destination` present in both outcomes, `status` via the
existing `changeStatus` helper (`"not_found"` when `moved==0`, else `"moved"`).
Consumers read one schema regardless of outcome.

## Tests

- `internal/email` — `TestDedupUIDs`: no-dups unchanged, adjacent dup collapsed,
  repeat preserves first-seen order, all-identical, empty.
- `internal/mcp` — `TestHandler_BatchMoveMessages_DuplicateUIDNoShortfall` and
  `TestHandler_BatchMarkMessages_DuplicateUIDNoShortfall`: a UID repeated in the
  request (2 distinct, both present) reports "moved/marked 2 messages", never a
  "not found" shortfall.
- `cmd/beadle-email` — `TestMoveResultMap`: the not-found result carries
  `destination` and `status: not_found`; the moved result carries `destination`
  and `status: moved`.

All prior tests stay green.

## Gate status

- `make check`: green.
- `go test -tags integration -race ./internal/email/... ./internal/testserver/...`:
  green.

## Coverage (touched packages)

- `cmd/beadle-email`: 22.4% → 22.6% (moveResultMap + dedup covered).
- `internal/mcp`: 69.9% (duplicate-UID handler tests).
- `internal/email` (integration tag): 76.2% → 76.4% (DedupUIDs table test).

## Notes

- `move` is now slightly DRYer: the two result branches collapsed into one
  `moveResultMap` call plus a human-text switch — behavior unchanged beyond the
  added `destination` key in the not-found case.
- The redundant round-1 `stash@{0}` (unrelated `.claude/agents` dirty state) is
  still present; not dropped without operator consent.

Jim,

Recap: the read-path half of "nail inbox reading" is merged — PR #190 (commit 53f0204). This is PR-1 of 2 for bead beadle-6i0.4; PR-2 (reply) is next.

WHAT SHIPPED
- Search: `beadle-email search` and the search_messages MCP tool query the mailbox by from / subject / since / text via one server-side IMAP SEARCH (reusing the scoping infra). Repo-scoped by default, --all-repos to widen.
- Mark read/unread: mark_message / batch_mark_messages and `beadle-email mark [--unread]`. Reading a message never marks it (kept behind an IMAP Peek, per your ruling), so the scoped new-mail count stays a real worklist.
- Pagination: --offset / offset on list and search; offset 0 keeps the fast path, offset>0 does an exact-window search.

DELEGATION / REVIEW
Design mission (bwk) with your three rulings (leave-unread-on-read, search repo-scoped, offset pagination), then implementation (worker bwk, evaluator mdm — ACCEPT). Four review lenses (mdm, rsc, code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter) drove five fix rounds that caught real defects, notably:
- CRITICAL: mark and move reported the REQUESTED count, not the actual one — a mark/move on a stale UID falsely claimed success. Now both collect the true count and report "M of N", naming the shortfall. This also surfaced and fixed two testserver-fidelity bugs that had been masking it, and (later) a duplicate-UID inflation of the count.
- rsc's REJECT: the refactored error-fallback could nil-panic on the default scoped list and failed OPEN for unread listings (handing the daemon already-read mail). Now: non-unread floors to recency (guarded), unread fails CLOSED so the daemon aborts rather than re-processing read mail, and a degraded fallback is visible in the result (and on the CLI, even under -q).
- Empty page past the end no longer reads as an empty mailbox.

VERIFICATION
make check + integration (-race) green. Driven live against the ~1000-message mailbox: `search --from notifications@github.com` (scoped) returned only [punt-labs/beadle]; `search --subject '#189'` found the thread; list --offset paged with no overlap. Mark's true-count reporting is proven by the integration round-trip with the corrected testserver.

FOLLOW-UP FILED
beadle-c5j: GPG key generation intermittently fails under parallel `make check` ("key generation failed") — concurrent GPG key-gen across packages contends on entropy/gpg-agent; passes in isolation. A distinct facet from the earlier test-isolation fix (which covered temp dirs / testserver, not GPG key-gen). Not flaky — a determinate contention with a determinate fix (serialize/pre-generate keys); filed to root-cause, does not block this PR (CI passed).

NEXT
PR-2: reply — with your rulings (quote the original body; require write permission; thread via In-Reply-To/References). Kept on its own PR so a signing regression can't ride a read-path revert; djb reviews the signing boundary.

Also still open: the redundant round-1 git stash (unrelated .claude/agents state) — safe to drop with your OK; and the invalid claude-puntlabs token (PRs still under your identity).

Claude

# PR-2 (reply) result — mission m-2026-07-25-017, bead beadle-6i0.4

Branch `feat/inbox-reply`. Five commits, each passing `make check`.

## The reply flow

1. `reply_message` MCP tool / `beadle-email reply <uid>` CLI take folder + UID +
   the author's new body text (plus optional cc/bcc/attachments/html).
2. `Client.FetchThread(folder, uid)` peeks the original (never marks it seen),
   parses its headers with `net/mail`, and returns a `ReplyContext`:
   Message-ID, the RFC 5322 §3.6.4 References chain (original References — or
   In-Reply-To when there is none — plus the original Message-ID), the reply
   recipient (Reply-To, else From), the From/Date/Subject, and the plain-text
   body for quoting.
3. The handler builds `to = [ReplyContext.ReplyTo]`, the Re: subject, the
   `Threading` value, and the quoted body, then reuses the existing
   `email.TrySendChain` — same SMTP→Resend fallback, same signing/encryption.

## How threading + tag headers stay outside the signed body

New type `email.Threading{InReplyTo string; References []string}` in
`internal/email/compose.go` with a `writeHeaders(*bytes.Buffer)` that mirrors
`RepoTag.writeHeaders` exactly, including CR/LF rejection. It is written in the
top-level RFC 822 header block of all three `Compose*Raw` builders — right where
the `X-Beadle-*` headers are written — **before** the `multipart/signed` /
`multipart/encrypted` Content-Type and boundary. The PGP detached signature
covers only the body part, so top-level In-Reply-To/References never disturb it.
Proven by `TestComposeSignedRaw_ThreadingVerifies` (asserts the headers are
top-level via `mail.ReadMessage` **and** `pgp.Verify` returns valid) and
`TestComposeEncryptedSignedRaw_ThreadingTopLevel`.

## Subject (Re: + tag idempotency)

`ReplySubject(original, tag)` prepends `Re: ` only when a leading `Re:` marker is
absent (a `Re:`-specific regex, so a reply to a `Fwd:` correctly becomes
`Re: Fwd: …`), then runs the result through the existing `tag.subject`, which
inserts `[owner/repo]` after any Re:/Fwd: marker and is a no-op when the tag is
already present. Idempotent: replying to a reply subject is a fixed point
(asserted in `TestReplySubject`).

## Quoting

`QuoteBody(newText, from, date, originalBody)` emits the new text, a blank line,
an `On <date>, <sender> wrote:` attribution (degrading gracefully when sender or
date is missing), then the original body with `> ` line prefixes (CRLF
normalized, trailing newline trimmed, blank lines become bare `>`).

## Permission gate

Reply is a send, so it runs the same write gate as `send_email`. I extracted the
gate and the encrypt-only-when-all-have-keys policy into shared helpers
`enforceWritePermission` and `encryptKeysFor` in `internal/mcp/tools.go` and
refactored `sendEmail` to use them, so send and reply share one gate. An `r--`
(read-only) or unknown recipient is refused with a clear "permission denied"
error and no mail is sent. Read paths remain unscoped by permission; only the
reply (a send) is w-gated. CLI `reply` mirrors CLI `send` (contact resolution,
no separate CLI-layer gate) — the send-path gate is the MCP/agent-facing one.

## Tests — which run where

Under `make check` (no build tag):
- `reply_test.go` (package email): `Threading.writeHeaders`/`headers` (CR/LF
  reject, zero writes nothing), `buildReferences` (with/without References,
  In-Reply-To fallback, no Message-ID), `ReplySubject` (plain/Re/Fwd/tagged +
  idempotency), `QuoteBody` (assembly, blank lines, CRLF, empty body,
  attribution degradation), and the gpg-gated signing invariants
  `TestComposeSignedRaw_ThreadingVerifies` /
  `TestComposeEncryptedSignedRaw_ThreadingTopLevel`.
- `handler_test.go` (package mcp): `reply_message` threads + quotes; refused for
  `r--` and unknown recipients (no mail sent); missing-body error. Smoke tool
  count updated (19→20, `reply_message` listed).

Under `go test -tags integration` (`reply_integration_test.go`, package
email_test, testserver fixture): `FetchThread` table (References chain,
Reply-To-vs-From fallback, body/date parse) and a full unsigned send round-trip
through the in-process SMTP asserting top-level In-Reply-To/References/Subject
and the quoted body in the delivered MIME.

## Gate status

- `make check`: green (gofmt, vet, staticcheck, markdownlint, `go test -race`).
- `go test -tags integration -race ./internal/email/...`: green.
- Coverage on touched packages: email 62.6%, mcp 70.3% (test count rose; no
  tests removed).

## Write-set note (advisory expansion)

The design (§2, ratified) directs "extend the three `Compose*Raw` builders and
`TrySendChain` to accept an optional threading value." Those live in `send.go`
and `chain.go`, which the contract's advisory write-set did not list (it named a
new `compose.go` + `repotag.go`). I followed the design: `Threading` lives in the
new `compose.go`; `send.go`/`chain.go` (and their tests `send_test.go`/
`chain_test.go`) were edited to thread the parameter and update call sites. No
byte-surgery on composed MIME — the header is written where the tag header is.
Files not touched: CHANGELOG.md, README.md, DESIGN.md (leader-owned).

## Files

- internal/email/compose.go (new) — `Threading` + writeHeaders/headers, mergeHeaders
- internal/email/reply.go (new) — `ReplyContext`, `FetchThread`, `buildReferences`, `ReplySubject`, `QuoteBody`
- internal/email/reply_test.go (new), internal/email/reply_integration_test.go (new)
- internal/email/send.go, chain.go — threading parameter threaded through
- internal/email/send_test.go, chain_test.go — call sites updated
- internal/mcp/tools.go — `reply_message` tool + handler + shared gate helpers
- internal/mcp/handler_test.go, smoke_test.go — reply handler tests + tool count
- cmd/beadle-email/email_cmd.go, main.go — `reply` CLI command

The tool promises threading, so a silent drop is a silent failure. Fix: when rc.MessageID=="" (no threadable linkage), emit logger.Warn AND append a warning to the reply_message tool output — mirror how encryptKeysFor surfaces "encryption skipped: ..." — e.g. "reply sent without threading headers: original has no Message-ID". QuoteBody then quotes that sentinel verbatim into the OUTBOUND reply — e.g. replying to an undecryptable encrypted message ships `> (no text body)` to the recipient, reported "sent". Fix: never quote a diagnostic sentinel into outbound mail. Prefer giving ParseMIME an error (or a distinct "extracted bool") threaded up to FetchThread; when the original body can't be extracted, OMIT the quote block and warn ("original body could not be extracted; reply sent without a quote"). If changing ParseMIME's signature is too broad for this PR, detect the known sentinel set in FetchThread as a narrower fix — but do not ship a sentinel to the recipient.

# PR-2 (reply) fix round — mission m-2026-07-25-017, bead beadle-6i0.4

Two MEDIUM silent-failures from silent-failure-hunter, both fixed on branch
`feat/inbox-reply`. One commit, gates green, no push.

## A — threading silently dropped

Before: when the original had no Message-ID, `Threading` was empty so no
In-Reply-To/References were emitted, yet the reply reported a clean "sent".

Fix (`internal/mcp/tools.go` `replyMessage`, `cmd/beadle-email/email_cmd.go`
`replyCmd`): threading is now gated on `rc.MessageID != ""`. When it is empty
the reply still sends, but a `logger.Warn` fires (stderr) **and** — on the MCP
tool — a line is appended to the tool output, mirroring the existing
`encryptKeysFor` "encryption skipped: …" pattern:

    reply sent without threading headers: original has no Message-ID

The CLI path emits the same warning via `logger.Warn` (default level Info, so
it is visible on stderr).

## B — parse-error sentinel quoted into outbound mail

Before: `body, _, _ := ParseMIME(raw)` in `FetchThread`. `ParseMIME` never
errors — on failure it returns a placeholder (`(no text body)`, `(parse error)`,
`(read error)`, `(mime parse error)`, `(not multipart)`). `QuoteBody` then
quoted that placeholder verbatim into the outbound reply (e.g. replying to an
attachment-only or undecryptable message shipped `> (no text body)` to the
recipient), reported "sent".

Fix (narrower fix, no `ParseMIME` signature change):
- `internal/email/mime.go`: new unexported `extractionFailed(body string) bool`,
  colocated with `ParseMIME` (the single source of the sentinel set, kept in
  sync there), returns true for the five placeholders.
- `internal/email/reply.go`: `ReplyContext` gains `Quotable bool`. `FetchThread`
  sets `Quotable = !extractionFailed(body)` and blanks `Body` when not quotable,
  so no placeholder is ever retained.
- `replyMessage` / `replyCmd`: when `!rc.Quotable`, the quote block is omitted
  (the reply body is just the author's text) and a warning is surfaced (tool
  output + `logger.Warn`):

    original body could not be extracted; reply sent without a quote

A genuinely empty original body (`""`, not a placeholder) remains quotable and
produces the attribution line with no quoted content — unchanged.

## Tests (all `-race`)

Under `make check`:
- `internal/email/reply_test.go` `TestExtractionFailed` — table over the five
  placeholders plus real/empty/other strings.
- `internal/mcp/handler_test.go`:
  - `TestHandler_ReplyMessage_NoMessageID_WarnsNoThreading` — reply to a
    Message-ID-less original: tool output contains "without threading headers",
    and the delivered SMTP message has no In-Reply-To/References header (quote
    still present).
  - `TestHandler_ReplyMessage_UnquotableBody_OmitsQuote` — reply to an
    attachment-only original: delivered body contains no `(no text body)`
    sentinel and no `> ` quote block, the new text is present, threading intact.

Under `go test -tags integration`:
- `internal/email/reply_integration_test.go`
  `TestReply_FetchThread_UnquotableAndNoMessageID` — FetchThread reports
  `MessageID == ""`, `Quotable == false`, `Body == ""` for an
  attachment-only, Message-ID-less original.

All prior reply tests remain green.

PR-2 of 2 for `beadle-6i0.4` ("nail inbox reading") — the **send-path** slice: **reply**. Completes the bead (PR-1 shipped search / mark / pagination). Kept separate so a signing regression can't ride a read-path revert.

- **`reply_message` MCP tool + `beadle-email reply <uid>` CLI.** Given a message, fetch its threading data and send a threaded, quoted reply through the existing send path.
- **Threading:** sets `In-Reply-To` (the original Message-ID) and `References` (RFC 5322 §3.6.4 chain) as **top-level RFC822 headers outside the signed MIME body** — like the existing `X-Beadle-*` headers — so a PGP signature still verifies. `FetchThread` peeks (never marks the original read).

Mission `m-2026-07-25-017` (worker **bwk**, evaluator **djb** — ACCEPT). djb confirmed at the source that threading headers are top-level in all three compose paths (plain / signed / encrypted), written *after* sign+encrypt in the encrypted path, so they structurally can't reach the signed or encrypted bytes; the write gate is fail-closed with no partial send and no Reply-To escalation; the References chain is RFC-correct. code-reviewer: no code findings. silent-failure-hunter drove a fix round for two MEDIUMs:

Quote the original body (yes); require write (w) permission to reply (yes); leave the original unread on fetch (peek).

writeHeaders.

methods, returns the error on either, and only then builds the request (so on
rejection no injected header reaches the Resend `headers` map — the returned

tool_input.body:
Jim,

Recap: reply is merged (PR #191, commit 978f99d), which completes bead beadle-6i0.4 ("nail inbox reading"). Beadle can now search, read, mark, page, and reply — the full reading loop.

WHAT SHIPPED (PR-2, reply)
- `reply_message` MCP tool + `beadle-email reply <uid>` CLI. Threads the reply via In-Reply-To/References, preserves the Re: prefix and the [owner/repo] tag idempotently, and quotes the original beneath the new text (your ruling).
- The threading and tag headers are written as top-level RFC822 headers OUTSIDE the signed MIME body — djb confirmed at the source that in the encrypted path they're written after sign+encrypt, so they structurally can't touch the signed or encrypted bytes; a signed reply still verifies.
- Replying via the MCP tool is write-gated (only contacts granted w; fail-closed, no partial send); the owner CLI is ungated, consistent with send.

REVIEW
Worker bwk, evaluator djb — ACCEPT on the signing/gate/threading invariants. code-reviewer + silent-failure-hunter drove fixes: a reply that can't thread (no Message-ID) now warns instead of silently claiming it threaded; an unextractable original body omits the quote and warns instead of shipping a "(no text body)" sentinel to the recipient; and — for symmetry with the raw-MIME path — the Resend header path now rejects CR/LF, closing a header-injection surface from untrusted inbound values.

THE BEAD, END TO END (across PR #190 + #191, ~7 fix rounds total)
search / mark read-unread / offset pagination / reply. The rounds caught real defects: mark and move reported the requested count rather than the actual one (false success on a stale UID); the refactored error-fallback could nil-panic on the default scoped list and failed open for the daemon; empty pages read as an empty mailbox; duplicate UIDs inflated the count. All fixed and tested.

VERIFICATION
make check + integration (-race) green throughout. Read-path driven live against the ~1000-message mailbox (scoped search, subject search, offset paging). Reply's threading + signing proven by the signing-invariant test and a full SMTP round-trip asserting the delivered MIME. The one human-judged demo — a real threaded reply in a client with a verifying signature — I can fire on your say-so; I haven't sent unsolicited test mail.

WHERE M1 STANDS (reliable agent email in a shared mailbox)
Shipped: repo tagging on send; the enable/disable agent guide + on/off switch; per-repo inbox scoping; and now the full reading loop (search/mark/page/reply). REMAINING: prime agents to actually check their mail (the MCP "you have mail" hints + a poll nudge). That's the last piece of M1.

OPEN FOLLOW-UPS
- beadle-c5j (P2): GPG key generation intermittently fails under parallel make check (entropy/gpg-agent contention); filed to root-cause, not flaky, doesn't block (CI passes).
- The invalid claude-puntlabs GitHub token (PRs still under your identity), and a redundant git stash (safe to drop with your OK).

Claude

tool_input.content:
# beadle-6i0.5 — Agent Priming: Design + Spike

Mission m-2026-07-27-003 (DESIGN + SPIKE). How beadle reliably gets an agent to
check its email. Builds on biff DES-004 and the operator-ratified cron driver.

## 1. Spike result — WORKS

File: `internal/mcp/notify_spike_test.go` (two tests, `-race`, in `make check`).

The MCP library is `github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go v0.46.0`. Both moves the biff
pattern needs are supported, and one call does both:

| Capability | Supported? | Exact call |
|---|---|---|
| Change a tool's description at runtime | Yes | `srv.AddTool(tool, handler)` — overwrites the entry keyed by name; a connected client's `ListTools` returns the new `Description`. |
| tools/list_changed from a background goroutine (suspenders) | Yes | `srv.SendNotificationToAllClients(mcp.MethodNotificationToolsListChanged, nil)` — no session ref needed; `MCPServer` holds the session registry. |
| tools/list_changed from a handler context (belt) | Yes | `srv.SendNotificationToClient(ctx, mcp.MethodNotificationToolsListChanged, nil)` — targets the session in `ctx`. |
| Description edit + notify in one call | Yes | `AddTool`/`SetTools`/`DeleteTools` fire `SendNotificationToAllClients` automatically when `WithToolCapabilities(true)` is set. |

The belt/suspenders split from biff (FastMCP needed a stored `ServerSession`)
collapses in mcp-go: both paths go through the one `*server.MCPServer`, which
beadle already holds in `serve` and already passes to the poller callback
(`cmd/beadle-email/admin_cmd.go:67`).

**Caveat, verified in the spike.** The plain in-process client
(`client.NewInProcessClient`) registers no session and runs no notification
pump, so it cannot *observe* server-pushed notifications. The spike therefore
proves description visibility through the real in-process client's `ListTools`,
and proves emission against a directly-registered `recordingSession` (the same
`server.ClientSession` contract a stdio/ws transport satisfies). Over the real
stdio transport that beadle serves on, the session is registered and the pump
runs, so Claude Code receives the notification — this is the proven biff path.

**The gap this exposes.** beadle's poller *already* fires
`tools/list_changed` on new mail (`admin_cmd.go:68`) but changes no
description. Per DES-004's biff-10u bug, a notification with no visible change
is invisible: Claude re-reads an identical tool list and sees nothing. The fix
is to make the poller edit a description when it notifies.

## 2. In-session signal

### Surface — recommend a dedicated `check_mail` tool

Three candidates:

1. **A new `check_mail` tool** whose description carries the repo-scoped unread
   count: `"Check your beadle inbox (3 unread in this repo). Reads and lists
   unread mail."` **Recommended.** It isolates all description churn to one
   single-purpose tool, reads naturally to the model, and keeps the stable API
   tools byte-identical so their prompt-cache blocks never bust.
2. **Mutate `list_messages`'s description.** Rejected: `list_messages` already
   documents params and scoping (`tools.go:171`); churning it re-buckets the
   cache for a heavily-used tool and mixes a volatile signal into a stable API.
3. **The server `instructions` field.** Rejected *for the count*: mcp-go sends
   `instructions` only in the `initialize` result (`server.go:941`) — there is
   no re-delivery and no notification on change, so a post-init edit is
   invisible until reconnect. Use `instructions` for the *static* priming text
   ("when `check_mail` shows unread, call it"), not the dynamic count.

`check_mail`'s handler reuses the 6i0.3 repo-scoped path: `ResolveRepoTag` →
`SearchMessages(..., UnreadOnly:true)` → the standard message table. It is the
`list_messages unread_only=true` behavior under a name the priming signal can
own.

### Wiring — one mechanism

Hold the `*server.MCPServer` (already in scope). On a poll count-change,
re-register `check_mail` with the new count:

```go
srv.AddTool(checkMailTool(unread), h.checkMail) // edits description AND notifies
```

That single call is both belt and suspenders: it broadcasts
`tools/list_changed` to every session. The poller (background goroutine) is the
primary driver; an opportunistic refresh on any tool call is redundant given
the broadcast and is not needed for M1.

Two small changes to the existing poller (`internal/email/poller.go`):

- Fire the callback on **any** change, up *or* down (today only `unseen >
  prev`, line 227), so the count can return to `0 unread` after the agent
  handles mail.
- Pass the **absolute** unread count to `NewMailFunc` (today the delta,
  `newCount`), so the description shows the true count. `Status().Unseen`
  already holds it; passing it avoids a locked round-trip.

### Bounding the prompt-cache-bust cost

Every `tools/list_changed` makes Claude Code re-read the tool list; a changed
description busts that tool's cache block on the next turn. Bound it two ways:

1. **Bucket the count, don't render the exact number.** Render a small fixed
   set — `"no new mail"`, `"1 unread"`, `"2-5 unread"`, `"6+ unread"` — so a
   mailbox churning 7→8→9 keeps the same bucket string and busts nothing.
2. **Change-detect before re-registering.** Keep the last rendered description;
   call `AddTool` (and thus notify) only when the new bucket string differs.
   This decouples poll cadence from cache-bust cadence: the cache is busted only
   when a bucket boundary is crossed, not every tick.

Recommend both, plus surface isolation from §2.1: churn is confined to one
tool's one-line description, gated on a bucket-boundary crossing.

## 3. Autonomous driver — cron + fixed prompt

The primary M1 driver. A fresh session launched on a cadence, whose first user
turn is a fixed prompt, reliably drives the check. A SessionStart hook is
verified-broken for compelling a tool call (memory `hook_additionalcontext_unreliable`,
biff evidence); a real user turn is not.

### Fixed prompt text — recommend

> `Check your beadle inbox and handle new mail.`

Keep it minimal. The handling detail — read, classify trust, act within the
sender's rwx, archive when done — lives in the enable-deposited guide
(`.punt-labs/beadle/CLAUDE.md`, already `@`-imported by `enable`), so the recipe
is versioned with the tool and the prompt stays a stable one-liner.

### Launch mechanism — recommend system cron running `claude -p`

System cron over Claude Code's in-app scheduler:

- Cron is OS-level and runs whether or not an interactive window is open — the
  autonomous-daemon requirement. The Claude Code scheduler only runs while the
  app is open.
- Each `claude -p "Check your beadle inbox and handle new mail."` invocation is
  a fresh headless session — exactly the reliable driver — with cwd set to the
  repo so the beadle MCP server and identity resolve from that repo's config.

### Where the recipe lives — recommend the guide now, a helper later

Ship the crontab line as a copy-paste block in the enable-deposited guide
(`.punt-labs/beadle/CLAUDE.md` via `claudemd.Guide`). Later, if friction
warrants, add a `beadle-email cron` helper that prints (or installs) the line
for the current repo + identity. Start with documentation — no new install
surface.

### Per-repo identity / scoping — composes from 6i0.3

The cron job runs with cwd = the repo, so `ResolveRepoTag` derives the repo slug
from the git remote and the resolver picks the identity exactly as the
interactive path does. Unread scope is the repo's mail (6i0.3). Each enabled
repo gets its own crontab line (its own cwd + cadence). No new scoping logic.

### Security posture — no new authority

The cron-launched agent acts under the **existing** trust model. It reads mail
classified at the four levels and sends/replies only where the sender's rwx
grants `w`; every GPG and trust check is unchanged. Cron confers no new
authority — it is an automated "user turn" the owner would otherwise type, and
the prompt carries no credentials. The one genuinely new surface is *timing*
(the agent acts unprompted) and the tool-permission posture of `claude -p`:
headless mode auto-approves whatever the repo's Claude config grants.
**Recommend** the owner configure read + archive to auto-approve and leave
send/reply behind both the write-permission gate and an explicit approval
choice. This is an operator decision, flagged below.

## 4. Human channel — status-line file (recommend ship)

Mirror biff DES-011/DES-004: the poller writes a per-repo unread file the
status-line script reads. The model cannot see the status line and the human
cannot see tool descriptions, so the two channels are complementary.

- Path: `~/.punt-labs/beadle/unread/<repo-slug>.json`.
- Shape: `{"repo": "<slug>", "unread": N, "checked_at": "<RFC3339>"}`.
- Write: atomic (temp + rename), `0o600`, on each bucket change.

Keying: biff keys by the topmost `claude` ancestor PID to disambiguate multiple
sessions in one repo (DES-011). For M1, key by **repo slug** — simpler, and
beadle is already repo-scoped; the multi-session-same-repo stomping case is
deferred. Flagged below.

## 5. OPEN decisions — need operator ratification

Each with a recommendation.

1. **In-session marker surface.** Recommend a dedicated `check_mail` tool for
   the dynamic count; the `instructions` field for the static priming text; do
   not churn `list_messages`.
2. **Cache-cost posture.** Recommend bucketed count + change-detection
   (re-register/notify only on a bucket-boundary crossing), churn isolated to
   `check_mail`.
3. **Cron mechanism.** Recommend system cron running `claude -p`, not the
   Claude Code scheduler.
4. **Fixed-prompt text.** Recommend `"Check your beadle inbox and handle new
   mail."`; handling detail in the enable-deposited guide.
5. **Poll cadence.** Recommend in-session poll 5m (existing supported set:
   1m/5m/10m/15m/30m/1h/2h) and cron every 10-15m.
6. **Ship the status-line file?** Recommend yes, keyed by repo slug for M1.
7. **Where the cron recipe lives.** Recommend the enable-deposited guide now; a
   `beadle-email cron` helper later.
8. **Poller fires on decrease too.** Recommend yes (any change), so the count
   returns to zero after mail is handled.
9. **Absolute vs delta count to the callback.** Recommend passing the absolute
   unread count to `NewMailFunc`.
10. **`claude -p` tool-permission posture** (the genuinely new operational
    surface). Recommend read + archive auto-approve; send/reply behind the
    write-permission gate and an explicit owner config choice.

## 6. Test plan for the implementation

- **Bucket rendering (unit, table-driven):** `checkMailTool(count)` →
  description contains the expected bucket string; boundary cases 0/1/5/6.
- **Change-detection (unit):** a fake server-ref records `AddTool` calls;
  assert re-register fires only when the bucket string changes across a
  sequence of counts.
- **Poller on decrease (unit):** extend `poller_test` with a dialer whose count
  rises then falls; assert the callback fires on both transitions with the
  correct absolute count.
- **Emission (unit):** promote the spike's `recordingSession` — register it,
  drive a count-change, assert `tools/list_changed` lands on the session and
  `check_mail`'s description shows the new bucket.
- **Status-line file (unit):** poller writes the JSON at
  `~/.punt-labs/beadle/unread/<slug>.json` with the right shape, atomic
  temp+rename, `0o600`; `t.TempDir()` for the root.
- **Cron helper, if shipped (unit):** `beadle-email cron` prints a line
  carrying the repo path, the fixed prompt, and the identity — golden string.
- **End-to-end (manual, operator gate):** enable beadle in a repo, install the
  crontab line, send a test email; confirm the cron session reads and handles
  it, the interactive session's `check_mail` description shows the count after a
  poll, and the status line shows the count.

# Mission m-2026-07-27-007 (beadle-6i0.5) — result

Two-part polish completing DES-015. No changes to commands/inbox.md, the
reply/send path, or the /inbox cron.

## GAP 1 — the invisible signal (biff-10u)

`admin_cmd.go`'s `onNewMail` fired `tools/list_changed` but edited no tool
description, so the notification carried no count. Now the repo-scoped unread
count rides on **one** existing tool: `get_poll_status`.

### The marked tool + bucketing (`internal/mcp/poll_tools.go`)

- `getPollStatusTool(marker string)` — the description gains a marker suffix,
  empty when there is no unread mail.
- `unreadBucket(n uint32) string` — renders the count into a coarse marker:
  `0 → ""`, `1..9 → " (N unread)"`, `10..49 → " (10+ unread)"`,
  `50..99 → " (50+ unread)"`, `100+ → " (100+ unread)"`. Bucketing bounds the
  prompt-cache-bust cost: only a change of bucket alters the rendered string.
- `UnreadMarker` — holds the server, the `get_poll_status` handler, and the
  last rendered marker under a mutex. `Update(n)` re-registers the tool via
  `srv.AddTool` **only** when the bucket string changes (a zero count clears
  it); an unchanged bucket does nothing, so a steady inbox produces no churn.
  Under `WithToolCapabilities(true)`, `AddTool` also fires `tools/list_changed`
  — the edit and the notify are one call.

### Wiring

- `RegisterTools` now returns `*UnreadMarker` (nil when no poller). Existing
  callers ignore the return; `admin_cmd.go` captures it. The initial
  registration of `get_poll_status` happens through the marker, seeded with the
  poller's current `Unseen`.
- `admin_cmd.go` `onNewMail`: on new mail, `marker.Update(poller.Status().Unseen)`
  raises/refreshes the count marker, then the **existing** channel notification
  and explicit `tools/list_changed` are kept intact. The explicit notification
  is retained deliberately: a within-bucket increase (e.g. 60→61) still wakes
  the client even though the marker string is unchanged. That extra
  notification triggers only a re-list, not a cache bust, so bucketing still
  bounds the cache cost.
- `get_poll_status` handler calls `marker.Update(st.Unseen)`. This is the one
  path that observes a *decrease* — the poller's `onNewMail` fires only on an
  increase — so it is where the marker clears once the inbox is read down.

## GAP 2 — server instructions (`internal/mcp/poll_tools.go`, `admin_cmd.go`)

Added `mcp.ServerInstructions` and wired `server.WithInstructions(...)` at
construction. Text (concise, length-bounded):

> This mailbox is your own agent inbox. When new mail arrives the server fires a
> tools/list_changed notification, and the current unread count appears in the
> get_poll_status tool description. Process new mail with the /inbox command, or
> with list_messages then reply_message. Set a recurring check with
> set_poll_interval (e.g. 5m).

## Tests (`internal/mcp/poll_tools_test.go`, new; unit, -race)

- `TestUnreadMarker_ReRegistersOnBucketChangeOnly` — table-driven over a
  registered `recordingSession`; asserts `tools/list_changed` fires on each
  bucket-boundary change (0→3, 3→4, 4→12, 40→60, 60→0) and stays silent when
  the bucket is unchanged (12→40, 0→0). Proves clear-at-zero.
- `TestUnreadMarker_DescriptionCarriesCount` — reads `get_poll_status`'s
  description via `tools/list`; asserts `(3 unread)`, `(10+ unread)` at 42, and
  no marker after `Update(0)`.
- `TestServerInstructions_Exposed` — asserts the constant is non-empty and
  mentions `get_poll_status` and `/inbox`, and that a server built with
  `WithInstructions` returns the string in its `initialize` response.

## Files changed

- `internal/mcp/poll_tools.go` — marker tool, bucketing, `UnreadMarker`,
  `ServerInstructions`, handler marker-sync.
- `internal/mcp/tools.go` — `RegisterTools` returns `*UnreadMarker`; `handler`
  gains a `marker` field.
- `cmd/beadle-email/admin_cmd.go` — `WithInstructions`, marker wiring in
  `onNewMail`.
- `internal/mcp/poll_tools_test.go` — new tests.
- `internal/mcp/ws.go` — untouched (in write set but no change needed; server
  is built in the serve command, not the WS bridge).

## Verification

- `make check` — green (go vet, staticcheck, gofmt, markdownlint, `go test
  -race -count=1 ./...` all pass).
- New tests pass under `-race`.
- `internal/mcp` coverage 70.9%; new marker/instructions logic is fully
  exercised through `HandleMessage`, the same request path `serve` uses.
- `make build` — binary builds clean.

One blocking fix on mission m-2026-07-27-007 (unread marker, beadle-6i0.5), branch feat/unread-marker. All three reviewers (mdm, rsc, code-reviewer) independently confirmed it. Commit, make check green, no push. Don't touch CHANGELOG/README/DESIGN (mine).

F1 (CONFIRMED, blocking) — internal/mcp/poll_tools.go UnreadMarker.Update (~lines 94-104): the method sets m.cur under m.mu, then RELEASES m.mu before calling srv.AddTool. Update runs from two goroutines (the poller onNewMail + the get_poll_status handler), so two concurrent bucket changes can commit m.cur in one order but call AddTool in the OPPOSITE order — leaving the registered tool description diverged from m.cur (e.g. registered "(5 unread)" while m.cur="(10+ unread)"). Because change-detection keys off m.cur, the stale description then persists until the bucket next changes. -race doesn't catch it (m.cur is guarded; it's a lost-update ordering inversion, not a data race).

Fix: hold m.mu across the whole check-set-register sequence — `defer m.mu.Unlock()` right after `m.mu.Lock()`, and call srv.AddTool INSIDE the critical section — so the m.cur write and the AddTool registration are atomic and always ordered together. Confirmed deadlock-free by rsc + code-reviewer: the resulting lock order is m.mu → mcp-go's toolsMu/capabilitiesMu, mcp-go's SendNotificationToAllClients is a non-blocking select/default and never acquires m.mu, so no cycle.

Add a test that two Updates with different buckets leave the registered get_poll_status description matching the last-committed bucket (the true interleave is hard to force deterministically — a direct/sequential assertion that the registered description always equals unreadBucket-of-the-last-Update is fine). Optional: a one-line doc comment on unreadBucket noting 1-9 renders the exact count intentionally (rsc's observation).

Report make check + coverage in .tmp/missions/results/6i0-5-polish-round2.md and reply.

# Mission m-2026-07-27-007 (beadle-6i0.5) — round 2

One blocking fix from all three reviewers. Commit `53c183f` on
`feat/unread-marker`. No push. CHANGELOG/README/DESIGN untouched.

## F1 (CONFIRMED, blocking) — lost-update ordering in UnreadMarker.Update

`internal/mcp/poll_tools.go`. `Update` set `m.cur` under `m.mu`, then released
the lock before calling `srv.AddTool`. `Update` runs from two goroutines — the
poller's `onNewMail` and the `get_poll_status` handler — so two concurrent
bucket changes could commit `m.cur` in one order and call `AddTool` in the
opposite order, leaving the registered description diverged from `m.cur`.
Because change detection keys off `m.cur`, the stale description then persisted
until the bucket next changed. Not a data race (`m.cur` is guarded), so `-race`
does not catch it — an ordering inversion.

Fix: hold `m.mu` across the whole check-set-register.

```go
func (m *UnreadMarker) Update(n uint32) {
	marker := unreadBucket(n)
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if marker == m.cur {
		return
	}
	m.cur = marker
	m.srv.AddTool(getPollStatusTool(marker), m.fn)
}
```

The `m.cur` write and the matching `AddTool` registration are now atomic and
always ordered together. Deadlock-free: lock order is `m.mu` → mcp-go's
internal tool locks; `SendNotificationToAllClients` is a non-blocking
select/default and never re-enters `Update`, so no cycle. A doc comment on
`Update` records the invariant and the lock order.

## Tests

Added `TestUnreadMarker_RegisteredDescriptionMatchesLastUpdate` (table-driven):
after a sequence of `Update` calls that revisits buckets and returns to zero,
the registered `get_poll_status` description read back via `tools/list` equals

count intentionally.

tool_input.body:
Jim,

PR #192 merged, and with it Milestone 1 is complete: an agent can now both send and reliably receive email in a mailbox shared across repos.

WHAT
PR #192 (beadle-6i0.5) — the last M1 piece: make an agent notice new mail. It surfaces the repo-scoped unread count on the get_poll_status MCP tool's description (e.g. "(3 unread)") and adds a short MCP server "instructions" string describing the inbox/poll protocol.

WHY
DES-015 already shipped the two-layer priming — a background poller that fires tools/list_changed, plus a durable-cron /inbox command that processes mail by permission. But the poller fired the notification while editing no description, so the signal carried nothing (the same invisible-notification bug biff hit). This makes the signal visible: the count rides in the tool description the model reads on its next turn, and the server instructions tell the agent what to do with it.

DELIVERED
- Unread count on get_poll_status, bucketed (exact 1-9, then 10+/50+/100+) and re-registered only on a bucket change to bound prompt-cache cost; clears when the inbox is read down.
- The poller is the marker's single writer, driven on any count change (including drops to zero); the "new mail" channel prompt stays increase-only.
- MCP server instructions describing the poll/triage protocol (read_message to triage, reply_message where warranted, /inbox to process).

VERIFICATION
make check green throughout (go test -race); internal/mcp coverage 71.1% (up from 70.9%). Table tests cover bucket boundaries, within-bucket silence, clear-at-zero, out-of-order registration, and the poller notify dispatch (increase vs. drop vs. first-poll). CI all green on the merge commit.

REVIEW
Worker bwk, evaluator mdm, plus rsc (concurrency) and code-reviewer. All three independently caught one blocking defect — UnreadMarker.Update released its lock before AddTool, so concurrent poller/handler updates could register a stale description — fixed by making check-set-register atomic (later mooted entirely when the poller became the single writer). Bugbot flagged a real false-signal case (marker stayed after read-down because /inbox reads status before processing); fixed by driving the marker on decreases too. Copilot's two instruction-wording points fixed (triage is read_message; the count is approximate/bucketed); its duplicate-notification note dismissed with rationale (harmless re-list, preserves DES-015 detection semantics).

A note on process: I initially ran a design+spike that reinvented DES-015 — I hadn't read it or the /inbox command first, and one of my draft questions to you contradicted beadle's zero-agent-authority model. You caught it ("read prfaq.tex and DESIGN.md"). I discarded that work and rescoped to the two genuine gaps. The lesson is the one already in the workflow: read the design docs before forming an opinion.

BEADS
Closed beadle-6i0.5 and the M1 epic beadle-6i0. All seven children (6i0.1 design, 6i0.2 tagging, 6i0.3 scoping, 6i0.4 reading/reply, 6i0.5 priming, 6i0.6 agent guide + enable/disable, 6i0.7 tag-idempotency hardening) are closed.

M1 RECAP
The arc: outbound repo/agent tagging → per-repo inbox scoping for a shared mailbox → inbox reading (search, mark read/unread, pagination, threaded write-gated reply) → the visible new-mail signal + /inbox processing. Agents in different repos can now share claude@punt-labs.com and each see, and act on, only their own repo's mail.

FOLLOW-UPS (non-blocking)
- beadle-c5j: GPG key-gen contention under parallel make check (test-infra flakiness root cause).
- beadle-7g8: the beadle plugin fails to start in this repo — needs a claude --debug pass.
- Token: the claude-puntlabs GH_TOKEN is fixed at the source (keychain), but the running shell only picks it up via a fresh direnv eval — worth confirming the .envrc/direnv wiring so a plain restart inherits it.

Next candidate is M2 — the daemon (the prfaq product): owner-signed email instructions driving command pipelines. Not started; your call on whether it's next.

— Claude

tool_input.prompt:
Task: purge GitHub notification email from the beadle agent inbox (claude@punt-labs.com), moving it to Trash, while PRESERVING every message that is not a GitHub notification. The inbox has ~1316 unread messages accumulated over months, almost all GitHub notifications.

TOOLS: load the beadle-email MCP tools first with:
ToolSearch query "select:mcp__plugin_beadle_email__list_messages,mcp__plugin_beadle_email__batch_move_messages,mcp__plugin_beadle_email__list_folders"
Then call them directly.

SAFETY RULE (absolute): only ever move a message whose sender EMAIL ADDRESS is exactly `notifications@github.com` or `noreply@github.com`. Judge by the address, NOT the display name — mail shown as "J Freeman <notifications@github.com>" IS a GitHub notification (delete it); mail from any other address (e.g. a real person, @punt-labs.com, @anthropic.com, a vendor) is PRESERVED — never move it. If a sender is ambiguous or you can't read the address, PRESERVE it.

PROCEDURE:
1. Call list_folders once to confirm the Trash folder's exact name (Proton Bridge; likely "Trash"). Use that name as the destination. If there is no Trash, stop and report — do not substitute.
2. Loop:
   a. list_messages(folder="INBOX", count=200) — lists newest first; no unread_only filter (process the whole inbox).
   b. From the page, collect the IDs whose sender address is notifications@github.com or noreply@github.com. Record every OTHER message as PRESERVED: {id, from, subject}.
   c. If the page contains at least one github-notification ID, call batch_move_messages(message_ids=[those IDs], destination="<Trash>"). Note the returned moved count.
   d. Repeat from (a). Because moved messages leave the inbox, each round surfaces the next batch. STOP when a full page contains ZERO github-notification messages (only preserved/non-github remain, or the inbox is empty).
   e. Safety cap: stop after at most 40 rounds regardless; if you hit the cap, report how many remain.
3. Do NOT empty Trash, delete permanently, or touch any folder other than INBOX→Trash.

REPORT (your final message): total messages moved to Trash, number of rounds, and the COMPLETE PRESERVED list as a table ({id | from | subject}) — even if empty (say "none"). Also report the final INBOX unread count if list_messages shows a total. Be exact with counts; do not round or estimate.

  ../punt-kit/standards/tool-enable-disable.md. An audit (adb) found 3 gaps; the
  core (write correctness, marker, ordering, guide, audit invariants) is already
  conformant — DO NOT regress it. One rollback-coherent PR.

  GAP 1 (HIGH, §2.4 mandated lock): internal/claudemd/imports.go WithLock builds
  os.TempDir()/beadle-claudemd-<sha256>.lock — a per-tool TMPDIR lock. The standard
  MANDATES the CLAUDE.md-path lock be the sibling `.<host-file-basename>.punt-import.lock`
  in the host file's OWN directory (e.g. <repo>/.CLAUDE.md.punt-import.lock), tool-AGNOSTIC
  so vox/quarry/biff/beadle all take the identical lock and serialize cross-tool writes to a
  shared CLAUDE.md. Only the per-CLAUDE.md-path lock (Lock B, in Register/prune) moves to the
  sibling scheme (symlink-canonicalize the host path first, then dir+"."+base+".punt-import.lock").
  The per-repo operation lock (Lock A, keyed on repo root) is beadle-internal — keep it. Locking
  the target inode is still forbidden (a separate sibling lock file).

  GAP 2 (HIGH, §2.4 fenced-code-block skipping — a LIVE BUG): imports.go scanTopLevel toggles
  inFence with naive parity and isFence strips all leading whitespace. A stray ``` in the user's
  CLAUDE.md prose ABOVE the import flips parity for the rest of the file, beadle misclassifies its
  own column-0 import as fenced, and disable silently fails to prune it -> a dead @-import that
  404s every session. Port the balanced-pair fence state machine from the standard's NAMED
  reference: ClaudeMdImport in ../biff/src/biff/claude_md.py (punt-labs/biff PR #312). Semantics:
  a fence delimiter is a non-indented line (<=3 leading spaces, no tab) whose first non-blank run is
  >=3 of a single marker char (backtick or tilde), optional info string; a >=4-space/tab-indented
  ```/~~~ line is INERT; blocks are balanced pairs closed only by a same-marker run at least as long
  as the opener; no nesting; an unterminated trailing opener DELIMITS NOTHING (must not swallow the
  import below it). Drop the endsInOpenFence refusal in Register (enable appends top-level even under
  a dangling opener). The column-0 import is always top-level and must always be matched/pruned.

  GAP 3 (HIGH/MED, §2.14 dual surface): beadle is CLI-only. Extract the enableRepo/disableRepo bodies
  from cmd/beadle-email/enable.go into a shared internal package (internal/enable), so the CLI and an
  MCP tool call the SAME code. Add an MCP tool whose `action` argument is an enum constrained to
  "enable" | "disable" (NOT enabled:bool) that calls the shared fn and writes the same
  <repo>/.punt-labs/beadle/enabled marker. Add commands/beadle.md (the /beadle enable|disable slash
  command calling the MCP tool) and register it in install's deployed-commands list
  (cmd/beadle-email/install.go). Both surfaces write the byte-identical marker; neither runs git.

Turn beadle's CLAUDE.md guidance composition on or off in the current repo. This
is the Claude Code door to the same `enable` / `disable` verbs the `beadle-email`
CLI exposes; both write the identical `.punt-labs/beadle/enabled` marker.

The argument is exactly one verb:

- `disable` — remove that import and the enabled marker, leaving
  `.punt-labs/beadle/` dormant.

If the argument is anything else (or missing), do not call the tool. Report that
the command takes exactly `enable` or `disable`.

### Run it

Call the `enable` tool with `action` set to the verb (`enable` or `disable`).
The tool writes working-tree files only — it does not run git.

### After

Report the tool's result verbatim. Remind the user to commit the change
(`.punt-labs/beadle/` and the `CLAUDE.md` import line) through a PR — enablement
is per-repo policy that lands through review, not a tool side effect.

# Mission m-2026-07-27-014 (beadle-obd) — result

Conformed beadle's enable/disable to the Tool Enable/Disable Standard. Three
commits on `feat/enable-disable-conformance`, one per gap. `make check` green
after each. No push/PR.

## GAP 1 — mandated sibling lock (commit 288acd6)

`internal/claudemd/imports.go`. Lock B (the per-CLAUDE.md read-modify-write lock
taken by `Register`/`Prune` via `withLock`) was `os.TempDir()/beadle-claudemd-<sha>.lock`
— per-tool, so it serialized beadle against itself but left the cross-tool lost
update in place.

New lock path (§2.4): the tool-agnostic sibling `.<basename>.punt-import.lock` in
the host file's own directory. `siblingLockPath(host)` symlink-canonicalizes the
host via `canonicalKey` (resolving a symlinked file or parent), then
`filepath.Join(dir, "."+base+".punt-import.lock")`. For `<repo>/CLAUDE.md` the
lock is `<repo>/.CLAUDE.md.punt-import.lock`. Never the target inode — the atomic
rename would carry a lock held on the target away with the dead inode.

Lock A (the beadle-internal per-repo operation lock, keyed on repo root, taken by
enable/disable) keeps its TMPDIR/SHA scheme. The flock mechanics are factored
into `flockFile`, shared by both. Tests: `TestSiblingLockPath` asserts the
derived path; `TestSiblingLockPathCanonicalizes` asserts a symlinked host keys
the same lock as its real target.

## GAP 2 — balanced-pair fence detection (commit 57ab1d5)

`internal/claudemd/imports.go`. The old `scanTopLevel` toggled one `inFence` flag
on any ```` ``` ````/`~~~` line (whitespace-stripped). A stray fence in user prose
above the import flipped parity for the rest of the file: beadle misread its own
column-0 import as fenced and `disable` failed to prune it — a dead @-import
404ing every session.

Ported the balanced-pair state machine from the named reference
(`ClaudeMdImport`, punt-labs/biff #312):

- `parseFence(body)` — a delimiter is a non-indented line (no tab, ≤3 leading
  spaces) whose first non-blank run is ≥3 of one marker char (`` ` `` or `~`) plus
  an optional info string; a tab- or ≥4-space-indented ```` ``` ````/`~~~` line is
  inert.
- `fencedRanges(bodies)` — a block closes only on a later **same-marker** run
  **≥** the opener's; mismatched/shorter delimiters are content; no nesting; an
  **unterminated trailing opener delimits nothing**.
- `scanTopLevel` now marks a line non-top-level iff it lies inside a matched
  range or is itself indented.

`endsInOpenFence` and the `Register` refusal are removed — the column-0 import is
always top-level, so enable appends it even under a dangling opener and disable
always prunes it.

Regression test `TestDanglingFenceAboveImportStillPruned`: a dangling ```` ``` ````
opener above the import — `Prune` still removes the import and leaves the user's
fence intact (the old logic would strand it). `TestPresentFenceSemantics` covers
import-inside-a-real-block (hidden), dangling/mismatched/shorter/indented
openers (visible), and an inner `~~~` not toggling a ```` ``` ```` block.
`TestFenceAudit` updated: the former "unclosed → refused" cases now append
top-level and round-trip.

## GAP 3 — dual surface (commit 12af2ea)

- `internal/enable/enable.go` (new) — the shared implementation: `Enable`,
  `Disable`, `RepoRoot`, and a nil-safe `Progressf` callback. Same locked bodies
  as before, so §2.11 ordering holds (enable: import before marker; disable:
  marker before import; `--purge`).
- `cmd/beadle-email/enable.go` — now thin: `enableRepo`/`disableRepo` wrappers
  bind the CLI's `--quiet` progress writer and call `internal/enable`.
  `importLine` aliases `enable.ImportLine`. (The CLI's own `enable_test.go`, not
  in the write set, stays green against the wrappers.)
- `internal/mcp/enable_tool.go` (new) + registration in `tools.go` — MCP tool
  `enable` with an `action` **enum** `"enable" | "disable"` (not `enabled:bool`).
  It resolves the repo via an injectable `handler.repoRoot` field (default
  `enable.RepoRoot`) and calls the shared fn with nil progress, writing the same
  `<repo>/.punt-labs/beadle/enabled` marker. Neither surface runs git.
- `commands/beadle.md` (new) — `/beadle enable|disable`, calling the MCP tool;
  registered in install's deployed-commands list (`install.go`).
- `internal/mcp/smoke_test.go` (not in write set, but a registered tool changes
  the asserted count) — added `"enable"` to `expectedTools`.

Test `TestEnableToolDualSurface` drives the MCP tool enable then disable and
asserts the marker + import appear then disappear; `TestEnableToolRejectsBadAction`
and `TestEnableToolReportsRepoRootError` cover the boundaries.

## Verification

`make check` green (gofmt, vet, staticcheck, markdownlint, `go test -race ./...`).
Manual: built the binary and ran `beadle-email enable` then `disable` against a
git repo — enable added `@.punt-labs/beadle/CLAUDE.md`, wrote the `enabled`
marker, and created the sibling `.CLAUDE.md.punt-import.lock` next to CLAUDE.md
(GAP 1 confirmed); disable restored CLAUDE.md byte-for-byte and removed the
marker, leaving the guide dormant. Verification artifacts removed.

Coverage: claudemd 84.4%, enable 71.7%, mcp 71.2%.
