Jim,

Two merges this batch.

WHAT
- #193 — enabled biff for the beadle repo and refreshed its CI-notify workflow.
- #194 (beadle-obd) — conformed beadle's enable/disable to the Tool Enable/Disable standard, which was updated 2026-07-27, three days after beadle's enable/disable first shipped (#188).

WHY
biff enable was your direct request. For #194, an audit (adb) against the updated standard found three gaps — one of them a live bug.

DELIVERED
#193:
- The committed `.punt-labs/biff/enabled` marker + the `@`-import, so biff travels with the repo.
- Fixed `biff-notify.yml`: the refresh had it watching `Lint`/`Tests` — workflow names this repo does not have. Both reviewers (Cursor HIGH + Copilot) caught it; corrected to beadle's actual `Test`/`Docs`, so CI-failure notifications actually fire.

#194 — three gaps closed:
- Mandated sibling lock. The CLAUDE.md write lock moved from a per-tool TMPDIR path to the standard's tool-agnostic `.CLAUDE.md.punt-import.lock`, so beadle serializes against vox/quarry/biff editing the same CLAUDE.md instead of only against itself.
- Live disable bug fixed. The old fence scanner used naive parity: a stray code fence in your CLAUDE.md prose flipped classification, beadle misread its own import as fenced, and `disable` silently failed to remove it — a dead @-import that 404s every session. Replaced with the balanced-pair parser ported from biff's reference (a dangling opener delimits nothing). Regression tests both directions.
- Dual surface (§2.14). The enable/disable logic is now a shared internal package feeding both the CLI and a new MCP `enable` tool + a `/beadle enable|disable` command — both write the byte-identical marker; neither runs git.

VERIFICATION
make check green on both. #194 driven manually: enable added the import + marker + sibling lock; disable restored CLAUDE.md byte-for-byte and cleared the marker. Coverage claudemd 85.2%, enable 71.7%, mcp 71.3%.

REVIEW
#194 — worker bwk, evaluator rsc, plus code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, type-design-analyzer. rsc CONFIRMED both risky ports (fence state machine, sibling lock) faithful to biff's reference, every fidelity check passing. One fix round: stale doc comment, a duplicated repo-root resolver (single-sourced), a typed `action` enum, a nil-guard, an enable-direction test, zero discarded Close errors. Copilot + Bugbot clean on the merge commit.

BEADS
Closed beadle-obd. biff enable was a chore (no bead).

FOLLOW-UPS
- biff-side (needs a biff bead): biff does not symlink-canonicalize its CLAUDE.md lock path, so on a symlinked ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md biff and beadle would lock different files and fail to serialize cross-tool. beadle's canonicalization is the more-correct behavior; biff should adopt it to match the standard.
- Assumption to note: §2.4's "a dangling opener delimits nothing" is followed trusting that Claude Code's own @-import resolver uses the same rule — the tool side is tested; the resolver side is the standard's domain, not something beadle can verify.
- Still uncommitted: 18 .claude/agents/*.md files (an inlined make-check gate hook, dirty since session start, unrelated to either PR) — awaiting your call on whether to commit them.

Earlier this session M1 (reliable agent email, send + receive) shipped and was recapped separately (#192 + the epic). Next candidate remains M2 — the daemon.

— Claude

## What

Each of the 18 `.claude/agents/*.md` definitions carried a `Write|Edit` hook that shelled out to `.claude/hooks/make-check-gate.sh`. This inlines the gate logic directly into the hook command.

## Why

Removes the dependency on the external script. The inlined command:

- resolves the edited file path via `jq` (falls back to a full `make check` when `jq` or the path is unavailable),
- skips `.tmp/` and the `.punt-labs/ethos/` submodule,
- runs `make check` only for Go / build / config files (`*.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `go.work`, `Makefile`, `*.sh`, `*.yaml`, `*.yml`),
- exits 0 (no-op) for everything else.

## Scope

Tooling only — `.claude/agents/*.md` hook frontmatter. No product code, no behavior change to `beadle-email`. One identical line changed per file.

## Verification

`make check` green (go vet, staticcheck, markdownlint, `go test -race ./...` — all packages ok).

make-check-gate hook was inlined into the 18 agent definitions."""
from pathlib import Path

# Anchor: the vendored-skip branch immediately followed by the Go/config
# branch. We splice the markdown branch between them, matching the original
# make-check-gate.sh case order (.md before .go).
ANCHOR = r'.punt-labs/ethos/*) exit 0 ;; *.go|'
DOCS_BRANCH = (
    r'.punt-labs/ethos/*) exit 0 ;; '
    r'*.md|*.markdown) _out=$(cd \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\" && make docs 2>&1); '
    r'_rc=$?; if [ $_rc -ne 0 ]; then printf \'%s\\n\' \"$_out\" | tail -n 60 >&2; exit 2; fi; exit 0 ;; '
    r'*.go|'
)

agents = sorted(Path(".claude/agents").glob("*.md"))
changed = []
for f in agents:
    text = f.read_text()
    if ANCHOR not in text:
        print(f"SKIP (anchor missing): {f}")
        continue
    if r'make docs' in text:
        print(f"SKIP (already has docs branch): {f}")
        continue
    count = text.count(ANCHOR)
    if count != 1:
        print(f"WARN ({count} anchors): {f}")
    f.write_text(text.replace(ANCHOR, DOCS_BRANCH, 1))
    changed.append(f.name)

print(f"changed {len(changed)}: {', '.join(changed)}")
